response.final_analysis: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is primarily associated with deficiencies in vitamin K-dependent proteins, particularly Protein C. This is due to the imbalance created when Protein C levels drop rapidly upon the initiation of warfarin therapy, leading to a hypercoagulable state. While Protein S deficiency could also contribute, Protein C deficiency is more frequently reported and recognized in the context of this complication.
